tenures.note: Billed as arriving from World League Wrestling following that promotion's own closure, renewing a short-lived rivalry with Jamie Underwood; won the UWF Rampage Championship from Underwood by pinfall (a small package) in his own first UWF match on 16 October 2004, catching the champion turned away from the match to check on his own distracted "son." Retained the UWF Rampage Championship over Brian McKenzie by countout on 30 October 2004, after McKenzie abandoned the match to save tag partner Chris O'Brien from a backstage beating by Michael Bonn. Retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "The Walking Contradiction" Sabbath in a no-contest on 27 November 2004, after Jamie Underwood interfered with a steel chair; pulled Sabbath's own hand into a truce once Underwood accepted a Last Man Standing challenge for Rise to Power. Ran off Team Canada's own beatdown of "Hentai" Ryu Osawa and helped him to the back on 1 December 2004. On 11 December 2004, was reunited backstage with girlfriend Tami Haight, newly assigned to cover the UWF as a reporter, then retained the UWF Rampage Championship over "Mr. Main Event" Chris Douglas by pinfall (the Limelight) after Jason Keening's own ringside presence at the aisle distracted Douglas at the finish, reconciling briefly with Keening backstage afterward. Broke up a scuffle between Jason Keening, Alex Extreme, and the Mercenary outside a sports bar on 11 June 2005, vowing revenge on the Mercenary for costing him time on the shelf, then stole the Mercenary's own Haliburton briefcase during the Douglas-de Sade tag match's own post-match chaos. Reconciled backstage with brother-in-law Shaun Borders on 6 July 2005, then beat Tom Landis by pinfall (the Limelight) as Borders's own chosen opponent, after struggling with the Mercenary over a stolen briefcase and being saved from a sneak attack by Borders. Pulled from a fatal four-way for the North American Heavyweight Championship on 20 July 2005 by the Mercenary, who beat him at ringside with a framed portrait of his own girlfriend and an item Amanda Wells described as one of the Mercenary's own stolen adult diapers. Was confronted backstage by Jacob Drake on 23 July 2005 over a phone call, setting up a future match between them. Won the Cruiserweight Championship of the World from Jacob Drake by pinfall (the Cradle Shock through a Sears display case) on 6 August 2005 in a match turned Falls Count Anywhere by co-president Jessica Marshall.

name: Nick "The Nighthawk" Leshenn

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): reaches the final three of the 20-man Deadly Rumble. Final Fight (28 November 1999): fights Alex Martinez to a declared double advancement in a steel cage, then wins the eight-man Thunderdome match to take the Final Fight tournament.

caption: A rising star who reached the final three of the 1999 Deadly Rumble and won the Final Fight tournament outright, feuding across both cards with Alex Martinez without ever winning the DWO World Title.

name: Joan Osborne

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): interrupts the broadcast as President of Morality in the Media, is revealed as Dark Vanity's own mother, seizes the DWO presidency and has Owner Mike Bilodeau arrested by the show's end.

caption: The President of Morality in the Media and Dark Vanity's own mother, who seized the DWO presidency at Deadly Draw 2 and had Owner Mike Bilodeau arrested before the card's end.

name: "The Sunny Killer" Sandy Fox

caption: "The Sunny Killer" Sandy Fox, Dark Vanity's ex-wife and Matt Booth's wife, who advanced through the 1999 Deadly Rumble field and was widowed, then reunited, within the same year.

name: Kieran Erottika

name: Gorilla

name: Trixxxster

caption: A debuting hardcore wrestler who won the Deadly Draw 2 Lethal Ladder match for $100,000 and then betrayed his own partner, Scott Richards, to keep the money for himself.

name: Jesse "The Man" Muldoon

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): wins a Rookies-Must-Retire steel cage tag match with Candyman. Final Fight (28 November 1999): wins a controversial match after DWO Owner Mike Bilodeau secretly paid his opponent, Johnny Bodd, to lose, then reaches the Thunderdome final.

caption: A member of the Dysfunction stable who won a controversial Final Fight match after DWO Owner Mike Bilodeau paid his opponent to lose, then reached the Thunderdome elimination final.

name: Mother Madeline

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): at Sick Rick's side for his release from prison and his Deadly Rumble win. Final Fight (28 November 1999): hands Sick Rick brass knuckles during his losing DWO World Title defense.

caption: Sick Rick's own long-time manager, present at his side through his release from prison, his 1999 Deadly Rumble win, and his eventual loss of the DWO World Title at Final Fight.

name: "The Last American Bad Ass" Alex Martinez

tenures.source: Deadly Draw 2 (May 1999): wins the Lethal Millenium flag match with Sick Rick, then reaches the Deadly Rumble's final five before being eliminated by Apollo. Final Fight (28 November 1999): fights Nick Leshenn to a declared double advancement in a steel cage, then eliminates himself in the Thunderdome final so Leshenn cannot be firebombed to the ring below, only to firebomb the winner anyway.

tenures.note: Made his in-ring UWF debut teaming with Alex Extreme against Team Canada; ambushed by Tom Landis and Kari Stevens in the aisle before the bell and busted open with a chair, then legally pinned by Bob Jablonski after collapsing from exhaustion mid-comeback, never having tagged into the match. Beat Scott "Hotspot" Daniels by pinfall (a Firebomb Chokeslam) in a Gold Rush dream match on 5 June 2004, surviving a low blow, a brass-knuckles punch, two steel chair shots, and a Pridebreaker. Beat "Dark Horse" Randall Osbourne by pinfall (a Firebomb Chokeslam) on 25 August 2004 after surviving a Tree of Woe facebite; cut a backstage promo naming Osbourne's own past in a rival promotion beforehand. His "Singles War" against Michael Augustine was never brought under control and ended without a decision on 18 September 2004 after the Privateers and Alex Extreme turned the brawl into a four-man fight. Teamed with the Sons of Cacaphony to beat the Universal Powers and Randall Osbourne on 22 September 2004, days after a backstage tryout of Erik and Chad Grimsson ended in a three-way handshake; combined with Erik Grimsson for a version of the Harlequins' own Reality Check on Todd Franklin for the pin. Lost a Tower of Doom cage match on 30 October 2004 alongside Quinn Brown, Uriah Hawkins, and Alex Extreme to the team of Edmond Winston IV, Victor Frost, Papa Legba, and Luke Kinsey, inadvertently costing his own side the match when he hurled Edmond Winston IV clear of the top cage's own door, completing Winston's team's own escape; joined the others in a post-bell beatdown of Winston with his own solid gold knuckles. Teamed with "Mr. Excitement" Alex Extreme in an impromptu, no-contest challenge for the UWF World Tag Team Championship against the Privateers on 13 November 2004, hitting a Firebomb of his own on Jacob Drake before "Agony" Michael Augustine's interference ended the match. Challenged Kyle Lee for the UWF World Heavyweight Championship on 11 December 2004 and lost by pinfall (a surprise inside cradle) after his own left knee buckled mid-move, denying Luke Kinsey a title shot of his own at Rise to Power. Vowed on 11 June 2005 to stop brooding over a loss to Luke Kinsey, then lost by pinfall to "Violent" Victor Frost (a chair-assisted spike piledriver, feet on the ropes) after Roxy Mayhem's own early bell rang stole a Firebomb Chokeslam win from him; walked away from the crowd's calls for revenge with visible restraint. Drank with the Mercenary, Alex Extreme, and the Sons of Cacophony at a Memphis club on 22 June 2005. Won the Road to the Gold Battle Royal to become the number one contender to the World Heavyweight Championship, then shared a beer and a truce backstage with Chris O'Brien on 6 July 2005. Delivered a vengeful promo about Daniel Kidd's own pipe attack on his knee backstage to open the 23 July 2005 broadcast, then teamed with Brett Greene in the main event, saving him from a Pride beatdown mid-show before Scott Daniels turned on Greene late in their own tag match. Beat Daniel Kidd by disqualification on 3 August 2005 after Cornerstones interference, saved by a returning Youth Gone Wild; appeared on the Greene Room on 6 August 2005, promising Brett Greene a future title shot if he won the World Heavyweight Championship at Gold Rush. Opened Saturday Night Rampage on 18 March 2006 celebrating the World Heavyweight Championship alongside the Sons of Cacophony and Alex Extreme, promised Brett Greene the first shot at his title, then saw Becky Byers turn that into a four-way match the following week against Greene, Luke Kinsey, and Alex Extreme.
